title: Branching, Switching & The HEAD Pointer
description: Understand lightweight branches as movable pointers, inspect the HEAD reference, and switch contexts with git switch.

blocks.content:
## What is a Git Branch?

In older version control systems, creating a branch required copying the entire project folder. In Git, a branch is simply a lightweight, movable pointer to a 40-character commit hash.

Because branches are just small pointer files inside `.git/refs/heads/`, creating, deleting, or switching branches is instantaneous and takes almost no disk space.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C1["C1"] <-- C2["C2"] <-- C3["C3"]
    Main["main branch pointer"] --> C3
    HEAD["HEAD"] --> Main
```

## Understanding HEAD

`HEAD` is a special reference pointer indicating which commit or branch your working directory currently reflects. Most of the time, `HEAD` points to a branch name, which in turn points to the latest commit.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    HEAD["HEAD (Current Context)"] --> Feature["feature branch pointer"]
    Feature --> C4["Commit 4 (Latest snapshot)"]
    Main["main branch pointer"] --> C3["Commit 3"]
    C4 --> C3
```

### Detached HEAD State

If you check out a specific commit directly instead of a branch name (`git checkout 3a91c8`), HEAD points directly to a commit rather than a branch. Commits made in detached HEAD state are not tracked by any branch and may be lost unless given a new branch name.

## Branch Operations with `git branch` and `git switch`

Git 2.23 separated branch switching from file discarding by introducing `git switch`:

```bash
# List all local branches (* marks current branch)
git branch

# Create a new branch without switching to it
git branch feature-auth

# Switch to an existing branch
git switch feature-auth

# Create AND switch to a new branch in one command
git switch -c feature-auth
# (Traditional equivalent: git checkout -b feature-auth)

# Switch back to the previous branch
git switch -
```

### Deleting Branches

```bash
# Safely delete a branch (prevents deletion if unmerged)
git branch -d feature-auth

# Force delete a branch (discards unmerged commits)
git branch -D feature-auth
```

## Branch Divergence

When multiple developers or feature branches commit independently, the history graph branches into parallel paths:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C1["C1"] --> C2["C2"]
    C2 --> C3["C3 (main)"]
    C2 --> C4["C4"]
    C4 --> C5["C5 (feature-payment)"]
```

Branch isolation allows developers to test experiments safely without disturbing the main line of development.

blocks.question: What physically constitutes a Git branch inside the .git directory?
options: A full duplicate copy of every tracked file in the repository
A 41-byte text file containing the SHA commit hash it points to
A database index stored on the remote host
A temporary zip archive generated by the compiler
blocks.explanation: A Git branch is simply a reference pointer (stored under .git/refs/heads/) containing the 40-character commit SHA plus a newline character.

blocks.question: Which modern command creates and immediately switches to a new branch called 'feature-billing'?
blocks.explanation: 'git switch -c <name>' creates and switches to a new branch in a single command (equivalent to 'git checkout -b <name>').
